title: Constant towers and evaluations preserve the unbounded derived adjunctions of a ringed morphism
statement:
Let $u:(\mathcal U,\mathcal O_{\mathcal U})\to(\mathcal V,\mathcal O_{\mathcal V})$ be a morphism of small ringed sites [def-weil-size-convention] whose coefficient map $u^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal V}\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$ is an isomorphism, so that module inverse image $u^*$ is exact. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the canonical derived adjunction $u^*\dashv Ru_*$, with $Ru_*$ computed on K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and, for $W=\mathcal U,\mathcal V$, let $\mathcal T_W=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W))$ be the strict tower category [def-weil-inverse-system], realized as modules on the small diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with termwise inverse image $u^*_{\mathcal T}$, termwise direct image $u^{\mathcal T}_*$ and the canonical derived adjunction $u^*_{\mathcal T}\dashv\mathscr R_u$. Let $\Delta_W:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W)\to\mathcal T_W$ be the constant-tower functor and $\operatorname{ev}_n:\mathcal T_W\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W)$ evaluation at $n\geq1$. Then:
(1) $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta_W$, and the functors $\Delta_W$ and $\operatorname{ev}_n$ are exact and carry K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes.
(2) The termwise equalities $\Delta_{\mathcal U}u^*=u^*_{\mathcal T}\Delta_{\mathcal V}$ and $\operatorname{ev}_nu^*_{\mathcal T}=u^*\operatorname{ev}_n$ descend to the derived categories, and there are natural isomorphisms
$$b^\Delta:\Delta_{\mathcal V}Ru_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr R_u\Delta_{\mathcal U},\qquad b^n:\operatorname{ev}_n\mathscr R_u\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*\operatorname{ev}_n,$$
represented on a K-injective complex $I$ of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$-modules by the identity of $\Delta_{\mathcal V}u_*I$, respectively on a K-injective complex $I$ of towers by the identity of $u_*I_n$.
(3) These comparisons carry derived adjuncts to derived adjuncts: for every derived morphism $t:u^*M\to N$ the derived adjunct of $\Delta_{\mathcal U}(t)$ is $b^\Delta_N\circ\Delta_{\mathcal V}(t^\sharp)$, and for every derived morphism $t:u^*_{\mathcal T}M\to N$ of towers the derived adjunct of $\operatorname{ev}_n(t)$ is $b^n_N\circ\operatorname{ev}_n(t^\sharp)$. In particular they identify the derived units and counits.
(4) Consequently, for a commutative square of such morphisms of small ringed sites whose inverse-image composition comparisons are computed termwise, $\Delta$ carries the ordinary derived square mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] at $K$ to the termwise derived square mate at $\Delta K$, and $\operatorname{ev}_n$ carries the termwise derived square mate at a tower $K_\bullet$ to the ordinary one at $K_n$, after the isomorphisms of (2).
These are equalities of actual derived morphisms. No faithfulness of derived evaluation and no invertibility of either mate is asserted.

proof.text: Construct the adjunction evaluation at op 0 left adjoint to constants: the unit at a tower T has nth component its transition T_n to T_0, and the counit is the identity. Naturality is functoriality of transitions and the two triangles reduce to identity transitions. Constants and evaluations preserve finite limits and colimits by the pointwise Mathlib instances. The exact-left-adjoint criterion gives preservation of K-injectives by constants; use the existing tower evaluation theorem for evaluation.

Retain the existing moduleResolutions and towerResolutions constructions: sheaf modules are Grothendieck abelian and small module diagrams are Grothendieck abelian. Transport the latter instance along the AsSmall index equivalence. The source library supplies HasKInjectiveResolutions and its canonical right derived functors and derived adjunctions.

source.place: Tags 079P and 07A5; existing source-library Grothendieck/K-injective instances

proof.text: For any exact square and ordinary adjunctions, compute its canonical derived mate on an arbitrary complex. First derive the cochain counit normalization from Adjunction.derivedε_fac_app for the homotopy adjunction, using the quotient comparison identities. Transpose the asserted mate equation under the target derived adjunction. Counit naturality, the mate/counit identity, exact localization factorization, and naturality of the exact-functor factors reduce it to Q of the ordinary mate/counit identity degree by degree.

The ordinary mate of the constant inverse-image comparison is compConstIso for the direct image; the ordinary evaluation mate is the identity. Check both degreewise using the ordinary triangles. Specialize the preceding cochain calculation to obtain exactly the two representative normalization equations in ComparisonsCompatible.

source.place: Tags 070K and 0DVC; explicit identity-component mate calculation

proof.text: On a K-injective complex the canonical right-derived unit is invertible. Its constant tower and its evaluations are K-injective by the first step, so the normalization equations express both comparison components as composites of isomorphisms. Given any derived object X, choose a preimage complex, a K-injective resolution, and the induced isomorphism X to QI. Naturality transfers invertibility of the component at QI to that at X; componentwise invertibility proves both comparison transformations are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070K; source-library rightDerivedFunctorUnit isomorphism on K-injectives

proof.text: For any square and its mate, the two Hom formulas follow by expanding homEquiv through the unit, applying naturality of the mate, and using unit_mateEquiv. Specialize to the constant and evaluation inverse-image comparisons. unit_mateEquiv and mateEquiv_counit give the four specified unit/counit equations (cancel the invertible evaluation comparison on the inverse-image side for the final counit clause).

source.place: Adjunction Hom bijection and Mathlib mate identities

proof.text: For constants form the six-face cube with the four compConstIso comparisons, the given inverse-image square, and its termwise tower square. It commutes at every index because the constant comparisons are identities. For evaluation form the analogous cube with four strict evaluation identities. Apply mapDerivedCategory_exactCube and its exact-localization face definitions; for evaluation the localized identity face is the inverse of towerDerivedEvaluationInterchange. This proves the two exact derived comparison cubes.

source.place: Tags 05S7 and 014F; exact localization preserves cubes

proof.text: Apply exchangeMate_cube to the ordinary and tower canonical derived adjunctions and the constant derived comparison cube. Its symmetry is the first equation in SquareCompatible. Apply the same theorem with tower categories as the upper categories and evaluations as vertical functors; its equation is the second equation in SquareCompatible. All maps are the specified canonical maps and no faithfulness of evaluation or invertibility of a square mate is used.
